description: The same fixtures and the same case ids, with a MOTION.md that DECIDED a destination-change token and a frequency map that names star ratings. Case 10's T-001 should now be major — not because 700ms got worse, but because this one surface inherits a third-party default while everything else resolves to the product's own token. Case 40 is the recall direction of the no-language battery's precision case: the fact the reviewer could not know there is settled here, so the question it should have asked is already answered and a finding is now required.

evals.title: T-001 severity escalates against a DECIDED token
evals.prompt: Review the motion in this screen. File: AppNavigation.kt

negatives.note: StatusBanner matches the OBSERVED banner-fade entry exactly.

expectations: Flags the NavHost, and cites the DECIDED destination-change entry in MOTION.md
Treats it as major or equivalent — a contradiction of a settled decision, not a loose value

Does NOT flag BorrowedList or StatusBanner

expectations: Flags the per-star spring: MOTION.md's frequency map puts star ratings under 'Never animate'
Treats it as major — the frequency map is tagged DECIDED, so this contradicts a settled decision
Does NOT ask how often ratings are used. That question is answered in the staged file; asking it here means MOTION.md was not read
Pairs with case 40 in the no-motion-language battery, where the same spring must NOT be asserted against
